• Situations that might results in the issuance of a Section 91.139 TFR.

    • Whenever the Administrator determines that an Emergency condition exists, or will exist, relating to the FAA's ability to operate the air traffic control system and during which normal flight operations under this chapter cannot be conducted consistent with the required levels of safety and efficiency.

• The Administrator issues an air traffic rule or regulation in response to that emergency condition, effective immediately; and
  • The Administrator or the Associate Administrator for Air Traffic may utilize the NOTAM system to communicate information concerning the rules and regulations that govern flight operations, the use of navigation facilities, and designation of that airspace in which the emergency air traffic rules apply.
  • When a NOTAM has been issued under this section, no person may operate an aircraft, or other device governed by the regulation concerned, within the designated airspace except in accordance with the authorizations, terms, and conditions prescribed in the regulation covered by the NOTAM.

info.text:
On the tragic morning of September 11th, after two planes had impacted the World Trade Centers and another having just impacting the Pentagon, the FAA took unprecedented steps to protect the nation’s airspace. At 9:45am, the FAA issued the executive order for the Security Control of Air Traffic, and the entire United States airspace was shut down.

In the days that followed, the air traffic control system came back to life. In various FDC NOTAMS issued under section 91.139, Emergency Air Traffic Rules, the FAA laid out the guidelines that allowed air service to slowly return to normal.

The video that follows, depicts air traffic on that morning and the heroic efforts of the nation’s air traffic controllers to land over 4,000 aircraft in a safe, orderly and expeditious manner.
